reason: Blocked A communicates a firm restriction and offers a clearly separate correction route. Birthday B gives the strongest task focus and keeps essential controls visible at both sizes. Neither reaches the requested threshold on the demonstrated evidence. Component tuples use the same six dimensions as the screen scores; null means the relevant behavior or visual state cannot meaningfully be graded here. Prototype overall scores normalize over applicable dimensions and therefore measure composition, not production readiness.
limitations: Inspected only the six attached images, checks.json and public/concepts/expansion-19.html. No implementation, delegation or prior ratings.

checks.json reports no overflow for all 12 candidate screen/size combinations, but contains no detailed action/result, keyboard, contrast, error-state or accessibility assertions. It does not prove vertical controls remain visible.

Candidate feedback/recovery scores are null for actual task outcomes: correction and Save only announce that this is a layout study. Structural recovery affordances are assessed under hierarchy and clarity. Missing runtime behavior is not treated as successful behavior or scored zero.
Baseline runtime credit rests on the supplied evidence summary, not a fresh drive. Its broader layout, reading and performance coverage does not establish the quality of every pictured control.
The prototype's 200% mode uses a CSS class, including explicit field stacking. This demonstrates that layout, not browser zoom, operating-system text scaling or native keyboard behavior.

No new hard-gate failure is established by the supplied evidence. Birthday C's below-fold action is a scrolling cost, not proof of an inaccessible primary control. Prototype readiness remains unproven.
Physical iPhone, VoiceOver, native interactions and representative novice use remain separate unverified gates. No full/native 9 or 10 certification is made.
